Introduction


While studying for CompTIA network+, I couldn't grasp the relationships between Transceiver and Fiber cable. 
Once I understood the structure, everything cleared up. So I decided to write it down.
In my last post, I introduced LAN cables (copper cables), which have a limited range.
LAN cable → Max 100m
Optical fiber  → A few kilometers to tens of kilometers

In an office use, it is enough to use LAN cable.
Switches and routers handle electrical signals internally. 
optical signal.
Electrical signal → Transceiver → Optical signal → Fiber Cable → Transceiver → Electrical

A Transceiver is a small module that plugs into a dedicated port called an SFP slot, found on switches and routers.

Switch

Last year when I was applying for jobs, my setup was a mess.
I had 10 tabs open, a spreadsheet to track applications, and multiple versions of my CV. Every time I wanted to tailor my CV for a role, I had to copy paste the job description somewhere, paste my CV somewhere else, and manually compare the two.

LangGraph State Machine Patterns — How to Stop AI Agents from Going Off-Script



  
  
  The "Agent Does Something Unexpected" Problem


LLM-powered agents that run outside their intended scope — infinite loops, unauthorized operations, non-interruptible processes. This happens when agent state management is implicit rather than defined.
LangGraph solves this with a graph-based state machine that makes state transitions explicit. Built on LangChain, it lets you define exactly which states exist and how the agent moves between them.



Concept
Description




State
Data structure the agent holds (TypedDict)


Node
Processing unit that transforms state (a function)


Edge
Transition rules between nodes (supports conditional branching)


Checkpoint
State snapshot for resume and rollback

articles.title: LangGraph State Machine Patterns — How to Stop AI Agents from Going Off-Script

articles.description:
How We Keep Quality in the Growing Roblox Marketplace (And Why We’re Hiring Moderators)
At KW Studio, moderation is a big deal. Every product that gets submitted is looked at closely. We check more than just how well it works; we also care about who really owns it. With so many sellers on the platform, making sure assets are truly owned and shared is super important for keeping trust in our marketplace.
This is where product moderators come in.
We offer guidance and training for our moderation system, but you need to have some experience with Roblox development. To really judge an asset, you’ve got to know how it works in a real game—how it’s built, organized, and optimized.
With KW Studio growing fast and more sellers joining, we’re seeing a lot more submissions. To keep up our quality, we’re looking for more moderators to help out.
As KW Studio Co-Founder Leonard Sandberg says:
“KW Studio is growing quickly, and with hundreds of sellers coming on board, we need more people to help us stick to our standards and make sure every product is up to par.”
If you’re interested in applying, it’s super easy. We don’t have a strict list of requirements to start with; we just want to know more about you, your experience as a Roblox developer, and why you think you’d be a good fit for moderating. No CV needed at this point.
Send your applications to:
legal@kwstudio.org
Check out our platform at  to see the kinds of assets we have and the quality we expect. This will help you figure out if the position fits your skills and experience.
KW Studio isn’t just about adding more products. We’re growing while keeping our quality high. That’s all thanks to our moderation efforts.
articles.title: KW Studio Hiring: How We Moderate a High-Quality Roblox Asset Marketplace
